> Shared AI work files carried passwords — and details the chat never showed

> A new study examined records people had published to let others inspect or replay an AI task. Those records held more than the answer on screen, and some included passwords and other private details. This does not mean ordinary private chats became public. The lesson is for anyone sharing AI work: send the checked result, not the whole work file.

strengthsObserved: The headline states the practical change directly and does not manufacture breaking urgency.
The opening identifies xAI, the early-beta audience, the connection path and the consequence before technical terms carry the reasoning.
The cloud-computer mechanism is connected to permissions, then applied in distinct work and personal examples.
The action list is concrete and proportionate; it does not pretend that a prompt or generic caution enforces access controls.
Uncertainty about credentials, retention, training and permission granularity is named rather than guessed.
